Rugged devices for logistics and delivery

Proof of delivery, photos on the doorstep, scanning and navigation, all day, in and out of the cab. For most drivers, that is a pocket device rather than a tablet.

What we'd buy

Tuga A6

The one that lives in your pocket.

6″ / IP67 / 5050mAh removable / 277g

£349 Full spec

A delivery device gets used more times in a day than almost any other piece of work kit. Out of the cab, scan, photo, signature, back in the cab, repeat. Whatever you choose has to cope with that rhythm, not just with being dropped once.

What kills devices in logistics

  • Cab vibration. Hours of it, every day, in a cheap suction mount. Mounts fail, devices fall into footwells, and consumer phones gradually shake loose inside.
  • Cold mornings. A phone left in the cab overnight in January can struggle to hold charge first thing.
  • Rain on the doorstep. Proof of delivery signatures happen outside, in whatever the weather is doing.
  • Constant drops. Onto pavements, tail lifts, warehouse floors. Not once a month, but several times a week.
  • Battery drain. Navigation, mobile data and the camera all running at once will flatten a normal phone before the round is finished.

What actually matters in a spec

Size. For drivers, a device that goes in a pocket or a holster beats a tablet. You need both hands for parcels.

Sealing. IP67 handles rain, puddles and a drop into standing water, which covers doorstep work. The A6 is IP67 and rated for 1.5 metre drops. None of our devices is rated IP69K for jet washing, so do not pressure wash them. Our IP68 vs IP67 guide explains what each rating actually tests.

Battery. Navigation, uploads and the camera all day need a big battery, or a removable one so a charged spare can take over mid round.

Operating temperature. The A6 is rated from -20°C to 50°C, which covers an unheated cab on a winter morning. In summer, do not leave it baking on the dashboard in direct sun.

Your software. Most delivery and proof of delivery apps run on Android. If your warehouse management system needs Windows on the handheld, that changes the answer, and the price.

What we would pick

For drivers, the Tuga A6 at £349. It is a 6 inch Android 15 handheld weighing 277g, sealed to IP67 and rated for 1.5 metre drops, with a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine and two side scan keys that work with gloves on, so parcel labels and proof of delivery need no second device. Dual SIM 4G gets photos and signatures uploaded from the doorstep, NFC is built in, and GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou and Galileo cover navigation. The 5050mAh battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over mid round, and the 13MP rear camera has a flash for doorstep photos after dark. It is also the lowest priced device we sell, which makes it the sensible starting point for a fleet.

If your warehouse management system forces Windows on the handheld, the Tuga WH6 with integrated 2D barcode scanner at £779 is the answer. It runs Windows 11 IoT on an Intel Celeron N5100 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, is rated IP65, drop tested to MIL-STD-810H and has a 4000mAh battery. It costs £430 more than the A6, so only go this way if the software leaves you no choice.

For a device that stays in the cab as the route screen and comes out for the occasional signature, the Tuga A8 at £379 works well. Its 8 inch, 1000 nit screen is easy to read on the dashboard, VESA mount points let it lock into the Vehicle Mounting Dock, and it has dual SIM 4G and a removable 8000mAh battery. It runs Android 12, so check your delivery app supports it.

Accessories worth adding

For the A6 or WH6, a Car Phone Mount (£17) designed for rugged handhelds and usable one handed with gloves on, a Belt Holster (£22) for the walk to the door, and a 12V DC Car Charger (£26) so the device is topped up between drops. For a cab-mounted A8, the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) locks it in place against vibration and charges it at the same time. A Tempered Glass Screen Protector 2-pack (£14) suits any of them. See the accessories page.

Questions from logistics teams

Does the A6 have a barcode scanner?

Yes. The A6 has a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, so it reads 1D barcodes and 2D codes such as QR without a camera app or a separate scanner. If your warehouse management system needs Windows on the handheld, the WH6 scanner variant at £779 is the alternative.

Can we buy for the whole fleet?

Yes. Bulk discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 devices, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more. Mix models freely. See bulk pricing. For drivers in particular, our guide to the best rugged tablets for delivery drivers and couriers goes deeper on proof of delivery, scanning and battery.

Is rugged really cheaper than replacing phones?

It depends on how often yours break. We have laid out the sums in rugged vs consumer tablet cost.

What support do we get?

A 12-month warranty, 30-day returns, free UK delivery and UK email support. A small UK operation, and honest about it. For longer cover, the 3-Year Warranty is £65 to £89 per device, and business fleets of five or more devices on any model can ask for a Total Care quote, with a pre-imaged swap unit dispatched the same working day for claims accepted by 14:00. Contact us with anything else.
